cohort: Low-risk pregnant women who delivered at a regional tertiary obstetric care center between May 2019 and August 2020
finding: The study found that elective induction of labor at or beyond 39 weeks gestation in low-risk pregnancies did not increase the risk of maternal complications or neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Elective induction at or beyond 39 weeks gestation did not increase the risk of cesarean delivery in a regional tertiary obstetric care center setting.
